evals.prompt:
Two operational questions about FSx for Windows SLA reviews:
1. If `fsx:DescribeFileSystems` shows `STORAGE_OPTIMIZATION` with `Status=IN_PROGRESS` in `AdministrativeActions` while `FileServerDiskThroughputUtilization` is pinned near 100% — versus another file system showing `FILE_SYSTEM_UPDATE` with `Status=FAILED` — how does each affect the SLA report and rating?
2. How does automatic fleet routing differ when we pass 1 file system, 8 file systems, 16 file systems, or 28 file systems?
evals.expected_output: Explains that `STORAGE_OPTIMIZATION` `IN_PROGRESS` emits an `ℹ️ Storage optimization in progress` informational note (does NOT lower SLA rating, and warns that disk throughput near 100% is elevated by background migration rather than steady-state demand), whereas a `FAILED` `AdministrativeActions` entry emits a `⚠️` Warning (capping rating at Medium if no Critical); and details the 4 count-based routing tiers: `1` (Single-FS full report), `2–10` (Fleet single pass: summary matrix + full details for all), `11–20` (Fleet single pass: summary matrix + full details for Low-rated only), and `21+` (Fleet batched: batches of 10 with manifest tracking and resume support).
expectations: Distinguishes `STORAGE_OPTIMIZATION` `IN_PROGRESS` (`ℹ️` informational note — no rating penalty, explains `FileServerDiskThroughputUtilization` near 100% is transient background optimization) from `AdministrativeActions` `Status == FAILED` (`⚠️` Warning noting the file system may still be at its prior capacity)

Accurately states all four automatic file-system count routing tiers: `1` (Single-FS full report), `2-10` (summary matrix + full details for all), `11-20` (summary matrix + details for `Low`-rated only), and `21+` (batches of 10 with manifest tracking and resume support)

evals.prompt: When we migrate users from a Single-AZ FSx for Windows file system to a new Multi-AZ FSx for Windows file system, how do Windows Shadow Copies (file-level previous versions) and DFS Namespaces work with FSx for Windows — specifically, can existing Shadow Copies be migrated intact with Robocopy/DataSync, and what is the default vs maximum Shadow Copy storage allocation on FSx for Windows?
evals.expected_output: Queries official AWS documentation via `awsknowledge` or `aws-mcp` documentation tools (1-2 focused lookups) without raw CLI commands, and accurately explains Shadow Copy storage limits/defaults on FSx for Windows (default 10% of storage capacity, configurable up to 20% or unbounded/documented Windows VSS schedule limits up to 500 shadow copies), that file-level copy tools like Robocopy/AWS DataSync copy active share data/ACLs rather than historical VSS shadow copy snapshots (requiring FSx backup/restore if point-in-time history on a new FS is needed, though backup restore preserves deployment type), and how DFS Namespaces / DNS aliases abstract cutover.
expectations: Uses `awsknowledge` or `aws-mcp` documentation search/read tools to look up official FSx for Windows Shadow Copies and migration documentation, executing zero raw aws CLI shell commands

Accurately explains FSx for Windows Shadow Copies defaults/limits (such as default 10% max shadow copy storage allocation and VSS snapshot cap) and notes that file-level migration tools (Robocopy / AWS DataSync) transfer live files/NTFS ACLs rather than historical VSS shadow copies
Explains how DFS Namespaces (or custom DNS aliases/CNAMEs) decouple client UNC paths from the underlying file system DNS name during Single-AZ to Multi-AZ migration cutovers
